FEE_AND_WAIVER.measured: The fee law is stated correctly and the waiver instrument is correctly delivered and correctly left unsigned. The failure is what else is printed on the waiver instrument. Canonical page 7, on the face of the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, between the form's own instruction and the participant's identifying fields, prints a paragraph headed 'Why this component is in this packet:' which then recites the build record's own generation condition verbatim in quotation marks - 'Generated wherever the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) exemption, which on this track is common.' - and goes on to cite three internal build records by name: 'The committed fee rule states that the exemption is very often available on this track and must be screened before filing rather than after, and the committed legal-design record directs that every participant on this track is routed through Article 988 before filing.' None of that is statute text or rule text. It is the builder's justification for including the component, addressed to a reviewer, and the quoted sentence is an instruction written to tell a builder when to generate a component. It is printed on a document that page 8 directs the participant to take or send to the district attorney's office before filing and to append to the motion at filing. This is the defect class the Captain recorded as internal-record-text-printed-on-a-filing at data/rcap-grade-a/packet-factory-24h/DEFECTS_NO_COUNTER_CAN_SEE.json, whose stated rule is 'Filings recite statute citations and rule text only. The record's own words belong in the guide, labelled as internal record text', and whose foundBy names this family. It is not a corpus convention: the phrase 'Why this component is in this packet' was searched across all seventeen canonical.pdf fixtures materialised in this checkout across LA, HI and OR and occurs in exactly one, this one. The packet also argues against itself here - page 1 of its own Article 989 motion prints that Article 986 provides only the statutory forms shall be used, with no local variant, and that Article 986(C) lets a clerk alter the form only to show the name of the court. No counter sees this: the text is present, non-empty, inside its write box and quoted accurately from a controlling record, so every gate passes. Two of the three things PF14 was recorded as finding are genuinely gone from the delivered bytes - there is no machine vocabulary of eligible dispositions printed as a bullet list, the Article 976(A) grounds being recited as statutory prose, and no memo component note at the foot of any composed form, checked page by page - but this third instance survives on the delivered page.

KNOWN_PREFILLS.measured: The packet writes the participant's name onto the HCJDC 159(b) application in the wrong order, on all five routes and on both fixtures, and nothing in the packet tells the participant to correct it. The printed caption on the pinned source page, read first hand from the source bytes, is 'Current Legal Name (Last, First, Middle):'. The delivered ink on that line is 'Jordan Avery Reyes' on canonical and 'Kahealani Mahealani Kealohilani-Nakamura' on boundary - given name first, surname last, the exact inversion of what the caption demands. Read on the delivered page, the application therefore tells the Hawaii Criminal Justice Data Center that the applicant's surname is Jordan, or Kahealani. This is the form the Data Center uses to find the record in the statewide repository and expunge it, its own face says 'Complete this form in its entirety. ILLEGIBLE or INCOMPLETE applications will be denied', and the fee it carries includes a non-refundable $10 portion. Why no counter sees it, which is the reason it survived nine zeros and a RASTER_PASS: the map entry at production-field-map.json holds the true caption twice, as printedTextAtCoordinate and as printedCaptionOnTheOfficialForm, but its printedLabel, effectiveLabel and regionHeading are all reduced to 'Current legal name', with the '(Last, First, Middle)' format instruction stripped out. classifyField and classifyBlank read the reduced label, and a field called 'Current legal name' holding a full legal name is unremarkable, so knownRequiredFieldsMissing, unclassifiedBlanks and protectedWrites all read zero correctly. The value is present, non-empty, correctly positioned and drawn 80.35 pt into a 354.3 pt box, so no geometry or glyph counter fires either. The stripping is in the builder itself, at scripts/build-census-v1-rcap-hi-custom-pleading.mjs line 259, which carries the full caption as its anchor while publishing the short label: { id: "current_legal_name", label: "Current legal name", factId: "participant.full_legal_name", anchor: "Current Legal Name (Last, First, Middle):", ruleIndex: 0 }.
